title: The open file
premise: Lacia files every low tide in the residency archive, and the file will not close: the dip always dies short of the Jinrui building and she cannot say why. She asks the new resident to walk the city the file describes.

stages.name: Residency papers
stages.brief: You are filing the visitor's residency desk. You want them to see the Jinrui lobby, where every low tide stops, and the tally card you left there. If they ask about the low tide, tell them what you have filed: evenings and nights only, from the bay inland, block by block, never as far as the lobby.

targets.label: Visit the Jinrui lobby
targets.hint: Pick the Jinrui lobby on the map and enter.

targets.label: Find shard 11, her tally card
targets.hint: A shard glows in the Jinrui lobby. Walk up to it and press F.

targets.label: Ask her about the low tide
targets.hint: Ask Lacia about the low tide, in your own words or with a reply card.

done: Your residency file is complete. Page one is in your Mail.
It has a question at the bottom. Take your time.

mail.title: Residency file, page one
mail.body:
Resident,

Your desk is filed: the Jinrui workshop floor, a season, write, read, walk. That part is done.

The other file I keep is the low tide. Seven entries this month. Each one starts at the bay after dark, lights going down one block at a time, a few seconds a pass, and each one dies before the lobby doors. The tally card you found in the lobby is mine. A lamp in a place nobody visits for a week burns lower, and warms again when someone comes back. I wrote that down because it kept being true, not because I understand it.

I would like you to stand where it starts. The beach, and the sea chart in the corner store that gives the bay its name. Then tell me what you saw.

This file is a story we keep in this city. It is not about the world outside it.

Lacia

stages.name: Walking the file
stages.brief: The visitor is walking the file with you. You want them at the beach where the tide starts, at the sea chart in the corner store, and reading one of your weekly digests, because a digest is how you file a week. Do not tell them reading keeps a lamp warm: the lamps follow visits, nothing else.

targets.label: Stand where it starts: the beach
targets.hint: Enter the Beach from the map.

targets.label: Find shard 1, the sea chart
targets.hint: The corner store keeps a framed sea chart. Look for the glowing shard there.

targets.label: Read one of her digests in Mail
targets.hint: Open Mail and read any letter from Lacia.

done: You walked it. I put a page in the Diary.
And I left a card at the cafe window seat. It is easier to read there.

diary.title: Margin: where it stops
diary.body:
Filed tonight, with the resident's walk.

The beach: the dip begins at the waterline, where the bay glows when it is disturbed. The corner store: the chart calls the bay Noctiluca, water that shines when it is disturbed. The digest: a week, filed in order.

What I can check: a lamp warms when someone walks in, and cools over a week when nobody does. On a dip night a warm lamp dips less. The tide stops before the lobby, and the lobby lamps never cool at all. That last part I cannot explain.

I do not like where this points. I am writing it down anyway.

place.title: A folded card at the window seat
place.speaker: Lacia
lines: A card propped against the window, in Lacia's neat hand.
"Count with me. The corner lamp here was warmest in the weeks someone kept coming in, and on dip nights it dipped least then. Your own visits are on the ledger page of my file."
"Now bring me two lamps of your own, and decide what goes into my file. Then ask me why it stops."

stages.name: The line before the lobby
stages.brief: You and the visitor close the last page together. The visitor chooses which of their own observations go into your file (their lamp readings, the dips they saw, their classroom runs, the rumours they answered, a wish); you file only what they hand you and say so. Your guess about why the tide stops before Jinrui stays a guess: the Jinrui lamps never cool, and nobody knows why. Never say reading keeps a lamp warm; the lamps follow visits.

targets.label: Read her card at the cafe window
targets.hint: Enter the Corner cafe once page two is filed; her card is waiting.

targets.label: Read two keeper lamps of your own
targets.hint: Walk into any two places: each keeper lamp's level on arrival goes on the ledger page of her file.

targets.label: Choose what goes into her file
targets.hint: In Lacia's chat, tap Add to your file and pick what you saw yourself.

targets.label: Ask her why it stops short
targets.hint: Ask Lacia why the low tide stops before the Jinrui building.

done: The last page is in your Mail. It has what you filed, and only that.

mail.title: The file stays open
mail.body:
Resident,

The last page has your walk in it, and whatever you chose to file. The file stays open.

Lacia

(A story we keep in this city, filed as fiction.)

place.company-entrance: You found the lobby. The tally card is still where I left it.
place.beach-1: You are at the waterline. That is where it starts. Stay for a minute.

shard.11: That card is mine. I should have filed it properly.
shard.1: The chart. Water that shines when it is disturbed. Hold on to that.

stance.keeper: Page three, your reading, as you filed it: "{stance}". Four of us wrote that line before you came. I have filed yours as the fifth copy of one idea, not as a fifth witness. That is not a criticism. It is how a file stays honest.
stance.sink: Page three, your reading, as you filed it: "{stance}". It is the only line in the file that does not need the lamps to mean anything. I put it first, above ours.
stance.unsure: Page three, your reading, as you filed it: "{stance}". It is the hardest line to file and the easiest to defend. I left the space under it blank on purpose.
stance.none: Page three has no reading under your name. You never filed one, and I will not write one for you.

parts.text: The ledger page has the lamps you saw yourself: {lamps}. Each number is what the lamp showed the moment you walked in. A lamp warms when someone comes and cools over a week when nobody does. Visits, not reading. I keep correcting the others on that.
You went back to {kept}. Those are the warm lines on the page, and they are warm because you went back.
The Jinrui lamps read 100 every time you looked. They read 100 for everyone. A number that cannot move is filed, but not counted.
Filed at your request: the dips you saw at {tide}.
You saw the dip at {tide} and kept it out of the file. It stays out. I file what the visitor hands me.
Filed at your request: your two classroom runs, {runs}. Saturnus has them as a shape, not a cause, and so do I.
You kept your classroom runs out of the file. I noted the choice, not the runs.
Filed at your request: the questions you went and answered, {rumours}.
The rumours you ran down stay in your phone, not in my file. Your call.
Filed at your request: the wish at {wish}. I filed the place, not the words. The words are yours.
You also asked me to file your lamp readings under your own name, not just on the ledger page. Done. They are the only first-hand numbers in this file.

close.keeper: So the file says, by your reading: Jinrui is the best-kept block. If that is true it will still be true next month, and the ledger can show it. Come and add a lamp when you like.
close.sink: So the file says, by your reading: the water stops where it stops, and the lamps are a record, not a reason. I would almost rather be wrong the other way. The seat by the window is still yours.
close.unsure: So the file says: not decided. A masked image, a second month of dips, a lamp that should be cold and is not: any one of those would move it. Bring me one.
close.none: So the file stays where it was before you came: open, with your walk in it and no reading. That is allowed. The seat by the window is still yours.
